geo.Olympic National Park: Olympic National Park has a rainforest, snowy mountains and wild beaches, all in one park.
geo.Mount Rainier National Park: Mount Rainier is a volcano with more glaciers than any other mountain in the lower 48 states.
geo.Crater Lake National Park: Crater Lake fills the top of a volcano that collapsed long ago. It's the deepest lake in the United States, almost 2,000 feet deep.
geo.Great Smoky Mountains National Park: Great Smoky Mountains is the most visited national park in the United States. The “smoke” is a natural mist that rises from its forests.
geo.Everglades National Park: The Everglades is the only place in the world where alligators and crocodiles live side by side.
geo.Acadia National Park: Acadia, on the rocky coast of Maine, was the first national park east of the Mississippi River.
geo.Shenandoah National Park: Skyline Drive runs the whole length of Shenandoah National Park, along the top of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
geo.Mammoth Cave National Park: Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world, with more than 400 miles of passages explored.
geo.Badlands National Park: The Badlands are full of fossils, from ancient rhinos and horses to saber-toothed cats.
geo.Death Valley National Park: Death Valley has the lowest point in North America, Badwater Basin, 282 feet below sea level.
geo.Joshua Tree National Park: Joshua Tree is where two deserts meet: the Mojave and the Sonoran. It's named for its spiky Joshua trees.
geo.Carlsbad Caverns National Park: On summer evenings, hundreds of thousands of bats fly out of Carlsbad Cavern to hunt for insects.
geo.Big Bend National Park: Big Bend sits in a huge bend of the Rio Grande, the river that forms the border between the United States and Mexico.
geo.Denali National Park: Denali National Park is home to the tallest mountain in North America, 20,310 feet high.
geo.Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park: Hawaiʻi Volcanoes has two of the most active volcanoes in the world, Kīlauea and Mauna Loa.
geo.Northeast: The Northeast has many of the oldest cities in the country, like Boston and Philadelphia, where the Declaration of Independence was signed.
geo.Southeast: The Southeast has warm weather, long beaches and the Great Smoky Mountains. Florida reaches farther south than any other state on the mainland.
geo.Midwest: The Midwest is called America's breadbasket because its farms grow so much corn, wheat and soybeans.
geo.Southwest: The Southwest has just four states, with deserts, canyons and Texas, the biggest state in the lower 48.
geo.West: The West has the tallest mountains, the biggest state (Alaska) and the only state made of islands (Hawaii).
geo.New York: New York is the biggest city in the United States. The Statue of Liberty stands in its harbor.
geo.Los Angeles: Los Angeles is the center of the movie business, in a neighborhood called Hollywood.
geo.Chicago: Chicago built one of the world's first skyscrapers, in 1885.
geo.Houston: Houston is home to NASA's Mission Control, which guides astronauts in space.
geo.Phoenix: Phoenix is one of the hottest big cities in the country. Summer days are often over 100°F.
geo.Philadelphia: The Declaration of Independence and the Constitution were both signed in Philadelphia.
geo.San Antonio: San Antonio is home to the Alamo, a famous old mission and fort from Texas history.
geo.San Diego: San Diego sits right next to the border with Mexico and is famous for its huge zoo.
geo.Dallas: Dallas grew up as a trading town for cotton and cattle. Now it's one of the biggest cities in Texas.
geo.San Francisco: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco was the longest suspension bridge in the world when it opened in 1937.
geo.Seattle: Seattle's Space Needle was built for the World's Fair in 1962.
geo.Denver: Denver is called the Mile High City because it sits about one mile above sea level.
Washington, D.C. is the nation's capital, home of the White House and the Capitol. It isn't part of any state.
geo.Boston: Boston had the first public school in America, opened in 1635.
geo.Miami: Miami is the only big US city that was started by a woman, Julia Tuttle.
geo.Atlanta: Atlanta has one of the busiest airports in the world.
geo.New Orleans: New Orleans is the birthplace of jazz music.
geo.Las Vegas: Las Vegas sits in the Mojave Desert and gets most of its water from Lake Mead, on the Colorado River.
geo.Detroit: Detroit is called the Motor City because so many cars have been built there.
geo.Minneapolis: Minneapolis has so many lakes that it's called the City of Lakes.
geo.St. Louis: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis is the tallest arch in the world, 630 feet high.
geo.Portland: Portland, Oregon, is famous for its rose gardens, so it's called the City of Roses.
geo.Nashville: Nashville is called Music City. It's the home of country music.
geo.Anchorage: Anchorage is Alaska's biggest city. Moose sometimes walk through its neighborhoods.
geo.Honolulu: Honolulu has the only royal palace in the United States, ʻIolani Palace.
geo.Cascade Range: The Cascades are a chain of volcanoes, including Mount St. Helens, which erupted in 1980.
geo.Great Plains: The Great Plains are wide, flat grasslands where millions of bison once roamed.
geo.Central Lowlands: The Central Lowlands have rich soil left behind by glaciers, which makes them great for farming.
geo.Coastal Plain: The Coastal Plain is low, flat land along the Atlantic Ocean and the Gulf of Mexico.
geo.Colorado Plateau: The Colorado River cut deep canyons into the Colorado Plateau, including the Grand Canyon.
geo.Great Basin: In the Great Basin, rivers never reach the ocean. Their water stays in lakes or dries up.
geo.Ozark Plateau: The Ozarks have thousands of caves and springs.
geo.Central Valley: California's Central Valley grows a big share of the fruits, nuts and vegetables eaten in the United States.
geo.Black Hills: Mount Rushmore, with four presidents' faces carved in stone, is in the Black Hills.
geo.Lake Okeechobee: Lake Okeechobee is the biggest lake in Florida. Its water flows south into the Everglades.
geo.Chesapeake Bay: Chesapeake Bay is the biggest estuary in the United States, famous for its blue crabs.
geo.San Francisco Bay: San Francisco Bay is one of the biggest natural harbors in the world, and Alcatraz Island sits in the middle of it.
geo.Gulf of Maine: The Gulf of Maine has some of the highest tides in the world, in its Bay of Fundy.
geo.Mississippi River: The Mississippi River runs from Minnesota all the way to the Gulf of Mexico. Together with the Missouri, it's one of the longest rivers in the world.
geo.Missouri River: The Missouri is the longest river in the United States. Lewis and Clark paddled up it on their famous journey west in 1804.
geo.Ohio River: The Ohio River starts in Pittsburgh, where two rivers meet, and flows into the Mississippi in Illinois.
geo.Colorado River: The Colorado River carved the Grand Canyon. Its water is used by about 40 million people in seven states.
geo.Rio Grande: The Rio Grande forms the border between Texas and Mexico. Its name means “big river” in Spanish.
